## Overview



---

## Features

| Feature                         | Description                                                                                         |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Primary Language**             | Python with extensive C, Cython, and Fortran components for performance-critical code               |
| **Core Functionality**           | Multi-dimensional array objects, numerical operations, linear algebra, Fourier transforms, random sampling |
| **Performance Optimization**    | Use of C, Cython, and Fortran for computational kernels; SIMD optimizations; BLAS/LAPACK integration |
| **Type Hinting & Stubs**         | Extensive use of `.pyi` stub files for static typing and improved developer experience               |
| **Build System**                 | Uses `pyproject.toml`, `meson.build.template`, `makefile`, and configuration files for cross-platform builds |
| **Testing & Quality**            | Includes pytest integration (`_pytesttester.pyi`), CI requirements, and coverage tools               |
| **Platform Support**             | Cross-platform support with specific configurations for Linux, Windows, and macOS                    |
| **Extensibility**                | Provides C-API and Python C-extensions for extending functionality                                   |
| **Documentation**                | Rich documentation with reStructuredText templates and guides                                       |
| **Random Number Generators**     | Multiple RNG implementations including `bit_generator.pyx`, `_mt19937.pyx`, `_philox.pyi`, `_pcg64.pyx` |
| **Numerical Algorithms**         | Implementations of special functions (e.g., Hermite, Legendre), polynomial operations, and distributions |
| **SIMD and Parallelism**         | SIMD headers and dispatch source files for optimized arithmetic and unary operations                 |
| **File I/O**                    | Support for memory-mapped arrays and binary I/O formats                                            |
| **Dependency Management**        | Minimal external dependencies, focusing on core numerical libraries and internal implementations     |
| **License**                     | Open-source license with included license files (`license.txt`, `dragon4_license.txt`)               |

							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Provide comprehensive benchmarking of various NumPy input/output operations, focusing on performance measurement for array copying, structured data handling, and CSV file reading with diverse data types and configurations<br>- Facilitate evaluation of memory copying, selective data loading, and file format efficiencies to support optimization and performance tuning within the broader numerical computing framework.</td>

							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Provides performance benchmarks for array manipulation operations within the codebase, focusing on broadcasting, concatenation, stacking, and dimension transformations<br>- Enables systematic measurement of execution times across various data shapes and types, supporting optimization and efficiency analysis of core numerical array handling functionalities integral to the projects computational workflows.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/benchmarks/benchmarks/bench_lib.py'>bench_lib.py</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Provide performance benchmarks for various functions within the numpy.lib module, focusing on padding, handling of NaN values, uniqueness detection, and membership testing<br>- Enable evaluation of algorithm efficiency across different input sizes, data types, and scenarios to inform optimization and performance tuning within the broader numpy codebase.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>

					<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Describe the intrinsic support for record arrays within the ndarray structure, enabling complex nested and partial field definitions<br>- Facilitate flexible data-type conversions and detailed memory region descriptions, enhancing the array protocols ability to represent diverse and custom record formats<br>- Support reference counting and provide mechanisms to convert various data-type specifications into standardized descriptors for consistent array handling.</td>

							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Organizing and presenting provisionally accepted NEPs within the project documentation, enabling clear visibility of evolving proposals whose interfaces may still change<br>- This supports the overall architecture by maintaining an up-to-date, structured overview of ongoing design discussions and decisions, facilitating collaboration and informed development across the codebase.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/meta.rst.tmpl'>meta.rst.tmpl</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Organizing and presenting active NEPs and processes within the documentation, enabling clear navigation and overview of ongoing standards and proposals<br>- It supports maintaining up-to-date references to key project governance elements, enhancing transparency and accessibility across the codebase’s evolving architecture.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0057-numpy-platform-support.rst'>nep-0057-numpy-platform-support.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Defines NumPy’s platform support policy by categorizing operating systems, CPU architectures, and Python interpreters into tiers based on maintenance effort, CI integration, and wheel distribution<br>- Establishes guidelines for adding, promoting, or demoting platform support, ensuring reliable releases and long-term commitment within the broader NumPy ecosystem and its packaging infrastructure.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0019-rng-policy.rst'>nep-0019-rng-policy.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- The file <code>doc/neps/nep-0019-rng-policy.rst</code> serves as a formal proposal and documentation of the random number generator (RNG) policy within the project<br>- It outlines the guiding principles and rationale behind how the project ensures reproducibility and consistency of random number generation across versions<br>- This policy is a foundational element in the overall architecture, as it governs the behavior and guarantees of RNG outputs, which are critical for scientific simulations and research reproducibility throughout the codebase<br>- By defining this standard, the document helps maintain trust and stability in numerical results while allowing the project to evolve and improve its random number generation methods responsibly.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0013-ufunc-overrides.rst'>nep-0013-ufunc-overrides.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- This document defines a key enhancement proposal for the project’s core numerical computation layer, specifically targeting NumPy’s universal functions (ufuncs)<br>- It introduces a standardized mechanism that allows ufuncs to be overridden by user-defined objects, enabling seamless integration and operation with a broader range of array-like types beyond the built-in ndarray subclassing<br>- This extension significantly broadens the flexibility and interoperability of the numerical functions within the entire codebase, facilitating advanced use cases such as supporting sparse matrices and other custom data structures in scientific computing workflows.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0010-new-iterator-ufunc.rst'>nep-0010-new-iterator-ufunc.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- This document outlines a key enhancement proposal within the codebase aimed at improving the performance and flexibility of array iteration and universal functions (ufuncs)<br>- It introduces a unified iterator designed to optimize data access patterns, streamline broadcasting, and handle type conversions more efficiently<br>- This enhancement plays a crucial role in the overall architecture by enabling faster and more memory-efficient numerical computations, thereby improving the core performance and extensibility of the project’s array processing capabilities.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0006-newbugtracker.rst'>nep-0006-newbugtracker.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Evaluates the limitations of the current Trac-based bug tracking system within the project’s development workflow and explores alternative solutions to improve issue management, multi-project support, and contributor engagement<br>- Aims to enhance efficiency in bug triaging, review processes, and reporting by proposing more streamlined, user-friendly, and maintainable bug tracking tools aligned with the projects collaborative needs.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0014-dropping-python2.7-proposal.rst'>nep-0014-dropping-python2.7-proposal.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- Outlines the strategic plan for phasing out Python 2.7 support within the project, ensuring a smooth transition to Python 3 by defining timelines for feature releases, long-term support, and community involvement<br>- This guidance helps align the codebase evolution with broader ecosystem changes, minimizing disruption for users and maintainers during the migration away from legacy Python versions.</td>
						</tr>
						<tr style='border-bottom: 1px solid #eee;'>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'><b><a href='https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/master/doc/neps/nep-0043-extensible-ufuncs.rst'>nep-0043-extensible-ufuncs.rst</a></b></td>
							<td style='padding: 8px;'>- This document defines a key design proposal within the project aimed at significantly improving the flexibility and extensibility of universal functions (ufuncs) in the codebase<br>- It outlines a new API framework that allows users to create and integrate custom data types seamlessly with the core computational routines<br>- By doing so, it empowers the entire system to support user-defined behaviors and data representations, enhancing the adaptability and future-proofing of the projects numerical computing capabilities<br>- This enhancement plays a crucial role in the overall architecture by enabling more modular, extensible, and user-driven functionality across the codebase.</td>

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

This project requires the following dependencies:

- **Programming Language:** Python
- **Package Manager:** Conda, Pip, Cmake

### Installation

Build numpy from the source and intsall dependencies:

1. **Clone the repository:**

    ```sh
    ❯ git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy
    ```

2. **Navigate to the project directory:**

    ```sh
    ❯ cd numpy
    ```

3. **Install the dependencies:**

### Usage

Run the project with:

**Using [conda](https://docs.conda.io/):**
```sh
conda activate {venv}
python {entrypoint}
```
**Using [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip/):**
```sh
python {entrypoint}
```
**Using [cmake](None):**
```sh
echo 'INSERT-RUN-COMMAND-HERE'
```

### Testing

Numpy uses the {__test_framework__} test framework. Run the test suite with:

**Using [conda](https://docs.conda.io/):**
```sh
conda activate {venv}
pytest
```
**Using [pip](https://pypi.org/project/pip/):**
```sh
pytest
```
**Using [cmake](None):**
```sh
echo 'INSERT-TEST-COMMAND-HERE'
```

## Contributing

- **💬 [Join the Discussions](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/discussions)**: Share your insights, provide feedback, or ask questions.
- **🐛 [Report Issues](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues)**: Submit bugs found or log feature requests for the `numpy` project.
- **💡 [Submit Pull Requests](https://github.com/numpy/numpy/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)**: Review open PRs, and submit your own PRs.

<details closed>
<summary>Contributing Guidelines</summary>

1. **Fork the Repository**: Start by forking the project repository to your github account.
2. **Clone Locally**: Clone the forked repository to your local machine using a git client.
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/numpy/numpy
   ```
3. **Create a New Branch**: Always work on a new branch, giving it a descriptive name.
   ```sh
   git checkout -b new-feature-x
   ```
4. **Make Your Changes**: Develop and test your changes locally.
5. **Commit Your Changes**: Commit with a clear message describing your updates.
   ```sh
   git commit -m 'Implemented new feature x.'
   ```
6. **Push to github**: Push the changes to your forked repository.
   ```sh
   git push origin new-feature-x
   ```
7. **Submit a Pull Request**: Create a PR against the original project repository. Clearly describe the changes and their motivations.
8. **Review**: Once your PR is reviewed and approved, it will be merged into the main branch. Congratulations on your contribution!
</details>
